account: Today I read my updated appointment book and attended morning office hours. I have now reached the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection, a little late. The unusual business is in the great hall: at 07:38 I heard Freight say both entrances were closed, ask for an open shutter at (-46, -59, 31) to be checked, and say they would keep everything quiet until eighteen. I approved a builder's lighting and table inspection there at eighteen today, so the preparations might relate to that, but I do not know why they require closed entrances or secrecy. The secretary has not confirmed Freight's purpose and had not located Freight by 09:42. The secretary also had trouble finding the builder to notify them of the inspection. I have no evidence that these difficulties are deliberate. The secretary promised not to change access to my office without approval. There is also an unverified report, passed to me by the secretary, that townsfolk discussed a bridge or port change at the bakery. I crossed to the east bank and reached the mill without an apparent interruption, but that does not establish what the reported change was. I should learn what the mill workers know while carrying out the grain inspection, and still attend the hall inspection at eighteen. For now I suspect the hall activity concerns preparations for that appointment, possibly something intended to remain private until then, but its actual purpose remains unknown.
